      Abstract
Higher-order logic and infinitary logic are two extensions of first-order logic that allow greater
expressivity. Both features have not been investigated together yet. In this paper, we define a
higher-order infinitary logic, based on an extension of simple type theory. The resulting logic features
higher-order quantifiers, infinite conjunctions and infinite disjunctions. We establish results at both
the syntactic and the semantic level. We introduce a sound notion of model, and we show a strong
version of completeness that entails the cut-elimination theorem for natural deduction. Moreover,
we prove an extension of Barr’s theorem, allowing us to constructivize classical proofs of a particular
fragment of higher-order infinitary logic.

 1      Introduction
Infinitary logic is an extension of first-order logic that allows infinite long statements or
proofs. This is typically achieved by featuring infinite sequences of conjunctions, disjunctions
or quantifiers. Such expressive powers are useful when axiomatizing various mathematical
concepts, but also when formalizing problems from graph theory or epistemic logic [30, 26].
Infinitary logic was first coined by Zermelo [37] for studying the foundations of set theory. It
was formally established by Karp [19] and its properties were investigated in [3, 20]. Among
those results is the cut-elimination theorem for infinitary logics [23, 34, 10, 36, 26].
    Geometric formulas are particular infinitary formulas, built using finite conjunctions,
infinite disjunctions and existential quantifiers. This is sufficient to formalize numerous
mathematical structures, like groups, rings and fields [30]. Geometric formulas satisfy an
interesting result of proof theory, known as Barr’s theorem. It states that any geometric
formula provable from a geometric theory using classical logic is also provable from the same
theory using intuitionistic logic. Originally expressed in topos-theoretic terms [2], it has been
proved in proof-theoretic terms [30, 26]. The original Barr’s theorem also claims to remove
the axiom of choice. Such an assertion has been investigated in [30].
    Higher-order logic [4] proposes another route to extend first-order logic and boost its
expressive powers. Rather than enhancing conjunction and disjunction, higher-order logic
focuses on the universal and existential quantifiers. While first-order quantifiers range over
individuals, higher-order quantifiers also have the ability to abstract over functions, predicates
or formulas. It follows that higher-order logic is highly expressive [9].

          Both infinitary and higher-order features have not been investigated together yet. In this
       paper, our aim is to define and study a higher-order infinitary logic.

       Contributions. The contribution of this paper is threefold. First, we extend simple type
       theory with a type, a constructor, and destructors for families of propositions indexed by an
       arbitrary countable set. We show that, in this setting, the β-reduction neither satisfies strong
       normalization nor confluence, but every well-typed term has a head normal form. Second,
       we define a higher-order infinitary logic, along with cut-free natural deduction inference
       rules. We define a sound notion of model and we prove a strong version of completeness that
       entails the cut-elimination theorem. Third, we show that Barr’s theorem can be extended to
       higher-order geometric theories, allowing us to constructivize classical proofs of higher-order
       geometric formulas.

       Outline. We present our extension of simple type theory with families of propositions
       in Section 2. We define higher-order infinitary logic and its natural deduction systems in
       Section 3. We prove the cut-elimination theorem in Section 4 and Barr’s theorem in Section 5.

        2     An Extension of Simple Type Theory
       Higher-order logic is usually modeled using Church’s simple type theory [4], where we have a
       type of propositions and a type of individuals (that are basic values). Here we want to model
       higher-order infinitary logic, that is to have an infinite conjunction and an infinite disjunction.
       In simple type theory, we cannot define functions taking infinitely many arguments. That is
       why we extend simple type theory with a new type for families of propositions indexed by an
       arbitrary countable set, along with a constructor and destructors.

intensionality, we wrap this idea with refinement of the V-complexes technique [29, 35, 1].

         5      Barr’s Theorem for Higher-Order Geometric Theories
        Geometric formulas are built using finite conjunctions, infinite disjunctions and existential
        quantifiers. Geometric implications are formulas of the form ∀⃗x.(A ⇒ B), where A and B
        are geometric formulas and ⃗x is a finite sequence of variables (possibly empty). A theory
        T is geometric when all its axioms are geometric implications. Barr’s theorem states that,
        in infinitary logic, any geometric implication that is classically provable in a geometric
        theory is also intuitionistically provable in the same theory. Note that the theorem refers to
        infinitary logic and not just geometric logic, because the principle of excluded middle cannot
        be expressed by a geometric formula or a geometric implication.

5.1        Friedman’s Translation for Higher-Order Infinitary Logic
Double-negation translations [21, 15, 12, 22] embed classical logic into intuitionistic logic by
applying the operator ¬¬A := (A ⇒ ⊥) ⇒ ⊥ at various places in formulas – depending on

Instead of applying ¬¬A := (A ⇒ ⊥) ⇒ ⊥, the parameterized translations apply the operator

We adapt it so that it takes into account infinite disjunctions.

 6     Conclusion and Future Work
We have extended simple type theory with a type, a constructor and destructors for families
of propositions indexed by an arbitrary countable set. In this setting, the β-reduction neither
satisfies strong normalization nor confluence. However, every well-typed term has a head
normal form. We used this type theory to define a higher-order infinitary logic. It features
higher-order quantifiers as well as conjunctions and disjunctions indexed by an arbitrary
countable set. We have defined a cut-free natural deduction system that precludes traditional
cuts and commutative cuts.
    We investigated the semantics of this higher-order infinitary logic. We have defined
a sound notion of model based on Heyting algebras, and we have shown a strong notion
of completeness based on V-complexes. These constructions allow us to derive the cut-
elimination theorem.
    Besides the elimination of cuts from proofs, we also studied the elimination of the principle
of excluded middle. We have extended Barr’s theorem to higher-order geometric theories. In
other words, we are able to turn any classical proof of a higher-order geometric formula from
a geometric theory into an intuitionistic proof of the same formula from the same theory.
    Barr’s theorem originates from topos theory, which can be used to give a semantics to many
logics. In particular, first-order geometric logic can be interpreted in a geometric category [25],
and higher-order logic can be interpreted in an elementary topos [18]. Grothendieck toposes
are both complete and co-complete geometric categories and elementary toposes. We could
thus investigate a semantics of higher-order infinitary logic in terms of Grothendieck toposes.
